6193.t: A variant of φυλή (phūlḗ, “tribe”), itself related to φύω (phúō, “to beget”).

6103.t: From σύμφωνος (sŭ́mphōnos, “agreeing in sound, harmonious”) + -ία (-ĭ́ā) and συν- (sŭn-, “with, together”) + -φωνία (-phōníā, “sound”).

6166.t: Neuter accusative plural of ταχύς (tăkhŭ́s, “quick”) used as adverb.

6129.t: The formation is similar to δάκτυλος (dáktulos) and κόνδυλος (kóndulos), probably first from a noun *σφόνδος (*sphóndos).

6198.t: From χαμαί (khamaí, “on the ground”) + λέων (léōn, “lion”); ultimately a calque of Akkadian 𒌨𒈤𒊭𒆠 (nēšu ša qaqqari, “chameleon, reptile”, literally “lion of the ground", "predator that crawls upon the ground”).

6168.t: From Proto-Indo-European *térmn̥, the same source of Latin terminus (“boundary, limit, end”).

6164.t: From Proto-Hellenic *tūrós (whence also Mycenaean Greek 𐀶𐀫 (tu-ro /⁠tūrós⁠/)), probably from Proto-Indo-European *tuh₂-ró-s, from *tewh₂- (“to swell”).

6170.t: From φαντός (phăntós, “visible”) + -άζω (-ắzō), verbal adjective of φαίνω (phaínō, “I cause to appear, bring to light”).

6138.t: From συντάσσω (suntássō, “to put together”) + -μα (-ma) and συν- (sun-) + τάγμα (tágma, “command, order”)

6108.t: From the aorist stem of συντρέχω (suntrékhō) + -η (-ē, verbal noun suffix).

6121.t: From συναλλάσσω (sŭnăllắssō, “to have dealings with another”) + -μα (-ma). By surface analysis, συν- (sun-, “syn-, with”) + ἄλλαγμα (állagma, “something taken in exchange”).

6175.t: Nominal form of the verb φθέγγομαι (phthéngomai, “to utter a sound, raise one's voice”).

6158.t: From τροπαῖος (tropaîos, “of defeat”), from τροπή (tropḗ, “rout, turning of an enemy”).

6184.t: From Proto-Hellenic *pʰrakʷjō, of unclear origin, with analysis complicated by the coexistence and apparent confluence of φρακ- (phrak-) and φαρκ- (phark-) in the verb's derivatives.

6165.t: From Proto-Hellenic *tótsos, earlier *tótyos, from Proto-Indo-European *tóti, adverb from *só. Cognate with Sanskrit तति (táti), Latin tot.

6151.t: From τοῖος (toîos, “such”) + -δε (-de, deictic suffix). Compare ὅδε (hóde, “this here”).

6174.t: From the root of φθέγγομαι (phthéngomai, “to make a sound”) + -μα (-ma).

6128.t: Unknown. Has been linked to Sanskrit स्फ्य (sphyá, “oar; spar”) and Proto-Germanic *spēnuz (“chip; shaving”), but this is phonologically impossible due to the aspirated labial /pʰ/ in Greek.

6187.t: From Proto-Indo-European *bʰerǵ- ~ *bʰreǵ- (“to roast, fry”), though the phonetics are irregular, suggesting a loanword from a third unidentified party.

6196.t: Borrowed from Biblical Hebrew חֶלְבְּנָה (ḥɛlbənɔ̂), from the root ח־ל־ב (ḥ-l-b) related to milk, from Proto-Semitic *ḥalīb- (“milk; fat”).

6127.t: Conventionally connected with Proto-Indo-European *sperH-, although Pre-Greek, according to Beekes.

6140.t: Possibly from Proto-Indo-European *ten- (“to stretch”); related to τείνω (teínō, “to stretch”). Cognate with Serbo-Croatian тѐтива, Slovene tetiva (< Proto-Slavic *tętiva), Polish ścięgno.

6189.t: From φυσάω (phūsáō, “to blow”) + -τήρ (-tḗr, agent noun suffix).

6144.t: From Proto-Indo-European *telh₂- (“to bear”) + -μων (-mōn), as its original meaning was "bearer".

6181.t: From the Pre-Greek root *φλυκτ- (*phlŭkt-) + -ις (-ĭs). Compare φλύκταινα (phlŭ́ktaină, “blister”).

6169.t: Unknown. This verb cannot be an old primary formation.

6159.t: Enlargement of τρύω (trúō), in the same manner as terms such as σμήχω (smḗkhō).
